title: Nonfiction
paragraphs: “That guy is…”
“What? Do you know him?”
“Um… it’s this guy named Takt who plays the Seven-Star Hero in *Faubrey*.”
“Huh… so he’s even appeared in a movie?”
“He’s the kind of guy who dabbles in all sorts of things, so I guess it’s possible…”

My Finacée is staring intently at my Rival. The Rival, on the other hand, is just giving a casual wave. By the way, it seems all of this footage was recorded using video crystals that the Rival secretly installed in various places. They’re set up all over the island, including in the mansion, and it looks like all of these clips were edited together from footage the Rival shot. Then Takt landed on the island and, well, went on a vacation of sorts.
“I don’t know how to put it… but they’re a bunch of lowlifes. They’re cackling about setting someone up… What an unpleasant start—I don’t even know who to root for.”

They’ve even added subtitles to the banners celebrating the expulsion of the Doctor so that his Father can understand them. The conversations of those pigs have been recorded as well. Oh, there’s a scene where they boast about stealing the Seven Star Weapons, a throwing weapon.

“This… it looks like they’re actually appearing and saying this themselves, but the story’s turned into one where they’re committing the major crime of killing the Hero and stealing the Seven Star Weapons, hasn’t it?”
“Theft… Motoyasu said something about that…”
“Huh? Really?”

The Finacée is watching the scenes of Takt and the others’ outrageous acts and bragging with a puzzled look on her face. Soon, it’ll move on to that creepy scene where they take turns handing over rings and kissing.
“What a sickening development. Don’t those guys question anything? I guess this is what they call a harem… but objectively speaking, it’s seriously disgusting…”
My father says this as if spitting out the words.
“It’s definitely unpleasant…”
“Oh my—a feast of carnal desire. Big Sister, I wouldn’t mind doing it with Naofumi-chan, you know?”
“I’m not actually going to do it, so don’t use this as an excuse to harass me.”
“Hmm? Mating? There’s a lot of it.”
Filo-tan tilts her head, looking confused as she munchs on popcorn. Father silently watches Filo-tan for a moment before turning his face back toward the screen.
“Are you going to make me watch a harem porn video featuring a bunch of lowlifes? If that’s the case, I’m leaving.”
“It won’t come to that, so I’d like you to stay and watch, okay?”
“Hmm…”

As we were talking, the background shifted to a scene in the sky foreshadowing a storm. Thunder roared, and Takt’s mansion was briefly shown at night. Then, the crimes committed by me and Rival began to play out. Just as a pig went “oink oink,” the island’s legend was clearly displayed on the screen.
“Hmm… a murder mystery… so it’s going the detective story route. I saw some ‘monster panic’ elements in the last woman’s corpse, but I guess that’s just foreshadowing.”

Then, they were discussing how all means of escape had been cut off. Of course, I was the one who destroyed them. The camera captured Takt and the others inspecting the destroyed boat and dock with an exquisite angle. Then, footage gradually begins to show pigs being found dead one after another on the island.

“There’s only one guy playing the detective role, but he’s acting strangely meta. Using Magic to blow away a storm at a time like this, or trying to escape from a closed circle—that’s a total red flag.”

Gradually, scenes of pigs being found dead and a section of the mansion being blown to bits by an explosion were interspersed, and the footage progressed to show Takt and the others being gradually cornered. There’s no scene of the maid pig committing the crime, is there? My heroic deeds aren’t depicted at all, either.
“It feels like, ‘Is Takt the Seven-Split Demon King?’ And is this heading toward the ‘everyone’s gone’ plotline?”
“Oh, I’ve heard of that before.”
His fiancée replied as if she’d definitely heard of it before. Big Sister looked on enviously at her fiancée and her future Father.
“Even with Magic, are there mystery stories like that in the other world too?”
“It’s one of the tales spread by a hero from the past.”
“Huh…”
“…I’d like to read all sorts of books, too.”
My Big Sister muttered quietly, her words tinged with resolve.
“Oh my—”
“Hm?”

It seems she’s frustrated in her own way that she can’t join the conversation. Big Sister is poking her with a finger in a teasing manner. Kou imitated Big Sister and poked my Big Sister from the opposite side of Big Sister.
“Big Sister, if you study too much, Father might get put off, you know?”
Vaguely, I recalled a time when Big Sister had been too eager to study and ended up putting Father off, leading to a mishap.
“If I remember correctly… just when things were getting cozy, she ended up saying a line she’d copied from a computer game in Father’s room or something like that.”
With a sharp jerk, Father turned his face toward me at incredible speed.
“…Are you saying there’s a world where Raphtalia rummaged through the contents of my computer?”
“Apparently so. It seems something happened because of what she found there…”
“Huh? Wait, what?”
It seemed like that put Big Sister in a bit of a bind… Did she lose somehow?
“What did she find out?”
“That’s something you absolutely must never find out, Raphtalia!”
“Y-yes!”
My Big Sister looks happy to be included in the group by Father. That’s great. I bet the Big Sister in my memories would smile unconsciously too. I’m a capable guy, after all.

Soon, the scene shifted to one where I was left speechless upon discovering the corpse of a shark-pig as it was about to head out into the open sea. Then… I’m not sure how it was edited, but it cut to a scene where Takt argued with a pig and took it down, and then the screen went dark as he ran through the pitch-black night searching for the culprit. From there, the plot took a sharp turn, shifting to a battle against the zombie pigs.

Then, just as the storm had passed and he was climbing up to the clock tower to call out to someone, the screen went dark. After a long list of character names and such scrolled by like the end credits, the island’s legend played again, concluding with the revelation that no one had survived.
The room brightened, and the screening ended.
“So, what did you think? Was it fun?”
“Nah… It’s more like a B-movie. The ending left me totally confused about what the point was. If it’s a mystery, it should stick to being a mystery.”
“Yeah, I get it. As Gaelion, I’d want to split it into multiple parts and reveal the truth that way.”
“That plot feels like something I’ve heard before. I don’t know whose idea it was… So, who’s the culprit?”
“Rival, my heroic moments aren’t in there!”
“It’s just the opening, so you don’t appear in it.”
That’s cruel! The scenes where I use my skills to wipe out the Takt crew were completely cut out during editing!
“So the unexpected twist is an outside culprit…?”
“It’s made so that doesn’t happen, so give it some thought.”
“What a pain… Either way, I feel like I’ve been forced to watch some weird movie. So, it’s a mystery, right? Even though it turned into a zombie panic.”
“It’s a non-fiction film designed to instill fear.”
“So it’s a documentary?”
My Father, who had been looking away as if annoyed, slowly turned his gaze toward us, then slowly turned it back toward my Big Sisters.
“…I see.”
That reaction doesn’t exactly seem like he doesn’t believe it, though.
“Um… so it’s true?”
My Finacée opened her mouth, as if searching for the right words.
“It’s a fact that Takt is truly an enemy of the world who possesses and hides multiple Seven Star Weapons.”
“We did it!”

Right now, Takt is at the Pig King’s place, getting a slave mark carved into him and being cuckolded. Apparently, he’s conducting a gathering of pigs scattered all over the world. By the way, I hear the Pig King was shown the footage uncensored. The Pig King was absolutely delighted to learn of Takt’s misdeeds. The Seven Stars Church has already detected the evidence, after all. Takt is the name of one who dies in agony! That expression, contorted with terror, is a sight to behold! My anger is far from subsided yet!
“It’s already been proven—he’s definitely headed for the pigsty!”
“I-I see…”
My finacée seemed at a loss for words as she stood next to Filo-tan.
“If Motoyasu-sama is appearing, I’d like to see it. I’m sure there’ll be a scene where he runs really fast.”
“Is that Yuki? He’s pretty tall and looks like a weirdo.”
“That’s rude to Yuki-chan, Rival.”
“Yes, yes.”
“You guys are a pretty dangerous bunch, aren’t you?”
“This is necessary, and I think it’ll be good for a bit of entertainment. Gaelion, you’ve more than earned the right to make money off those guys.”
“Are you planning to make a profit by broadcasting it worldwide?”
“Of course, the profits will be shared with Naofumi and the others.”
My future father is giving off major merchant vibes.
“Well, I don’t know if it’ll turn a profit, but why not?”
“Through this entertainment, I’d like you to ask the Spear Hero, Filolial, and the others for a favor.”
“No way.”
“Naofumi, this is necessary for business, so please just nod and agree.”
“What are we supposed to do?”
“Voice dubbing. The Filolials are great at impersonations, so if we do this, we can create all kinds of story variations.”
“I see… Motoyasu, give me a hand. That’ll make us some money.”
“Guh… Alright.”
Rival! You’re currying favor with my Father way too fast!

The rest is a story for another day. I hear that before Takt’s gang’s misdeeds were made public to the world, Takt’s pigs had mostly been rounded up and shipped off to the pigsty ruled by the Pig King. This footage was also sent to Mistira and her comrades, and it seems they were satisfied with the outcome.

Now, the story goes that after Takt’s sister recovered from her cold, she spent some time snooping around because she couldn’t track down her brother’s whereabouts. According to Rival, they were letting her run free as part of an experiment to see if those affected by Takt’s “breath” would change their ways or something like that.

Even after news of Takt’s misdeeds spread worldwide, she apparently continued to cause a huge commotion. Since Takt was the one at fault and his sister was treated as if she knew nothing about it, they didn’t exactly declare her innocent, but they did place her under house arrest. In the end, she didn’t reform at all; she attacked the castle guards while attempting to escape and ended up in the pigsty. It just goes to show—pigs are the only ones who get along with Takt!

The rest is a rather gruesome story. The movie about Takt’s downfall, released by Rival, became a worldwide hit. It was marketed as a mystery and a disaster film. Of course, everyone knew Takt was the villain, so it’s said that all sorts of spin-offs were created just to say, “Serves him right!” Rival produced a six-chapter series. The sales eventually made it a global phenomenon, and Rival became a billionaire. It’s so frustrating!

It’s been two weeks since Rival held that screening at the castle. Ren, Itsuki, and I are following the government’s orders to participate in waves across the country, gradually working to restore our reputations. Of course, it seems we’re each working on our own projects in between. My Father has begun rebuilding Big Sister’s village, just as originally planned. And of course, I hear he’s been buying up the village’s slaves and is steadily gathering them, or so they say.
“It feels like I’m being manipulated a bit, but this is a place where research is truly rewarding—I’m glad I’m here.”
“I was on my guard when I came here on his recommendation, but the research on modifying the Bio-Plant really saved the day.”

My father was absolutely delighted after completing the Bio-Plant-based house based on the research results, together with the Doctor. As for the Doctor, I heard that negotiations were finalized while our Rival was possessing Takt’s dragon. Apparently, he extended a helping hand just as the Doctor was at a loss in the research lab that had been destroyed due to the Takt faction’s power plays.
“Rat, you’ve got quite a large household—I hesitated about taking you in, but it turns out I made the right call.”

To gain the Doctor’s trust, the Rival had made it appear as though the monsters that were the subject of the Doctor’s research were dead, all the while protecting them. Upon reuniting with the monsters he’d believed to be dead, the Doctor decided to trust him, at least for the time being. What’s more, the government learned of the Takt faction’s misdeeds, and the Doctor’s lab—which had been slated for shutdown—was acquitted. Even so, it seems they came to my Father’s place. The monsters the Doctor brought along are certainly a group we haven’t seen around here before.
“At first, I wondered what that dragon with Takt was up to, but the fact is, it saved us. I’ve come to realize I should tone down my dislike of dragons a bit.”
“Come on, big sis, you should study hard. Gaelion will be watching over you.”
“Wait a minute… how long are you going to keep using Dad’s name?”
“Gaelion is Gaelion. It was named by my big sister from another loop.”
“Sigh…”

Meanwhile, Rival quickly had her Assistant brought in from the monster merchant and placed her under protection. From the assistant’s perspective, she was initially suspicious of this mysterious dragon impersonating her sister who’d died right before her eyes, but I hear she’s been accepting the situation quite a bit lately. As for Ren, she’s keeping her distance and avoiding getting too close. I hear she’s currently studying as an assistant to Doctor, in a way that’s similar to how things were in the first world.
“And then—”
She flinched at this point and turned her gaze toward the Mole the Rival had secured.
“How’s Imiya-neechan doing? You won’t grow any bigger unless you eat more, you know.”
“Uh, well…”

That rival of ours is surprisingly friendly toward the Mole. I wonder why he’s so concerned about the Mole’s well-being? The Mole, for its part, seems to be interacting with him as if it doesn’t quite understand why he’s taking such an interest.
